title: Lean core: the url facade leaves core
goal: Replace the url facade in GEMI's model download and origin checks and GMCP's content-URI validation and SSRF-guarded browse URL with in-tree std code that keeps url's behaviour on every input it accepts and refuses what it cannot parse exactly, then delete susi-vendor-url and lower the lean-core ceilings to the measured values.
host: CEO laptop, CachyOS Linux x86_64, 28 threads, other agents compiling
acceptance: cargo test --offline --locked -p susi --test architecture_tests --test orphan_sources --test lean_core_ceilings --test core_docs_promise_no_ui_or_plugins --test no_github_coupling --test task_records --test gmcp_requirements
scripts/gmcp-record-evidence.sh and --mastery on the committed tree

results.differential: susi_paths::weburl against url 2.5.8 (scratch harness, not committed): 400,000 clean http(s) inputs, 79,306 accepted, 0 differences in serialization, scheme, host, port, path, segments, query, fragment, and 79,305 origin-equality pairs equal; 800,000 noisy inputs (all schemes, whitespace, userinfo, IPv4/IPv6 forms, ports, dot segments), is_absolute_uri 0 differences except refusals of special-scheme hosts with non-ASCII text, % or xn-- labels (url accepts those through IDNA), and the strict parser never accepted an input url rejects. Frozen as 26 strict and 34 validity cases.
results.pillar_reach: to be measured on the merged tree
results.lines: susi-gmcp and susi-gemi-models shrink (measured on the merged tree)

limitations: WebUrl::parse refuses http(s) URLs a WHATWG parser would rewrite beyond case, default port, port zeros, empty path and IPv6 text: whitespace, controls, non-ASCII, backslash, userinfo, % or xn-- in the host, IPv4 not written as four plain decimals, dot segments, and chars that would be percent-encoded. Model downloads and the browse tool fail closed on those URLs with an error naming the reason.

is_absolute_uri answers false for a special-scheme URL whose host has non-ASCII text, a percent sign or an xn-- label (url accepts these through IDNA tables this code does not carry), so such MCP content URIs are now rejected.

Error texts changed: artifact_name and the browse tool report 'unsupported URL ...: <reason>' where url reported its own parse error or 'Expected HTTP(S) artifact URL' / 'SSRF BLOCK: scheme ... not allowed'.
